- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions at 5% of prior peak.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak within 3–5 days), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–4 day lag correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (alternating +/– 0.33), model tends to average out; avoid smoothing; use sentiment-weighted moving average for correction.
